prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: EN · Long headers, short data (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 5 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 13px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Region" · longest unbreakable word 44px · one-line width 44px
  col 2: header "Quarterly revenue (USD, millions)" · longest unbreakable word 60px · one-line width 212px
  col 3: header "Year-over-year growth rate" · longest unbreakable word 45px · one-line width 172px
  col 4: header "Number of active enterprise customers" · longest unbreakable word 67px · one-line width 248px
  col 5: header "Net promoter score" · longest unbreakable word 59px · one-line width 124px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 619px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 618px.
Fixed: content, font, 13px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Compare regional commercial performance across revenue, growth, enterprise customers and customer sentiment.","reading":"Readers scan each region across a row, then compare individual measures down their columns. The short body values leave room for headers to wrap without disrupting the data rows.","groups":["Revenue and year-over-year growth describe financial performance.","Enterprise customer count and net promoter score describe the customer base and its sentiment.","Region identifies each row and anchors comparisons across all four measures."],"keep_intact":["Region names and abbreviations","Numeric values, percentages and other individual data values","Whole words in headers"],"may_wrap":["Long headers can wrap at word boundaries; their shared header row can accommodate multiple lines."]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r2A: widths [65, 145, 130, 165, 113] · table 619×187px · row heights [53, 33, 33, 33, 33] · column headers wrapped 4/5 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2B: widths [65, 150, 125, 170, 108] · table 619×187px · row heights [53, 33, 33, 33, 33] · column headers wrapped 4/5 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
